title: When the rule fails

D0.outcome: States a positional rule, then names a feature whose change makes it fail.

D1.outcome: Given a familiar rule (knights before bishops; do not move a piece twice), finds a position where the exception applies and says which feature licenses it.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled one-feature minimal pairs, decides whether the rule applies and says why, and builds a minimal pair of his own for a rule.

D3.outcome: Predicts which rules survive a one-feature change and labels the rest as defaults with conditions.

misconceptions: A rule is either always true or useless.
conditions: A settled structure with known targets, a piece with a role in a coming attack, a pawn that needs support when advanced.
contrasts: Learning the rule as absolute and then being unable to find the 'ugly' good move.
Abandoning the rule after one exception.
An exception to a rule that does not govern the position.

soft_prereq_notes.OPN.TEMPO.D3: tempo-count exceptions are the first rules learners see fail

note: CD-4: exceptions and dynamic play are introduced from Tier 3 as D0-D1; tier 6 is where unlabeled use enters.
